'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*Aftermath of the [[Rwandan genocide]]
**A court in [[Rwanda]] finds [[Paul Rusesabagina]], a former hotel manager portrayed as a hero in the [[Hotel Rwanda|Hollywood film]] about the [[genocide]], guilty of [[terrorism]]-related [[criminal charge|charges]]. Rusesabagina, who remained handcuffed in court, denounced [[President of Rwanda|president]] [[Paul Kagame]] and said that he was abducted from [[exile]] in [[Dubai]] in order to stand trial in Rwanda. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/rwandan-court-finds-hotel-rwanda-film-hero-rusesabagina-guilty-terror-related-2021-09-20/ (Reuters)]
*[[Insurgency in Cabo Delgado]]
**[[Islamic State|ISIL]]-linked militants raid a village of [[Kagera (region)|Kagera]], [[Tanzania]], after crossing the border from [[Mozambique]], killing four people. Three of the victims were beheaded. Between 18 and 33 people have been kidnapped. [https://www.caboligado.com/reports/cabo-ligado-weekly-20-26-september-2021 (Cabo Ligado)]
*[[Anglophone Crisis]]
**Fifteen soldiers and civilians are killed during two [[bombing]] and [[shooting]] attacks in the [[Northwest Region (Cameroon)|Northwest Region]], [[Cameroon]]. The attacks had been carried out several days ago but were not reported until today. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/9/20/rebel-attacks-kill-15-soldiers-in-troubled-cameroon (Al Jazeera)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Volkswagen]] submits an offer of €2.5 billion for French car rental firm [[Europcar]]. The deal, which would give Volkswagen 66% of Europcar's shares, has been accepted by the board but still needs to be accepted by regulators in [[France]]. Volkswagen previously owned Europcar and sold it to French investment firm [[Eurazeo]] for €3.3 billion in 2006.  [https://www.rte.ie/news/business/2021/0920/1247953-volkswagen-europcar-offer/ (RTE)]	
*[[Twitter]] agrees to pay $809.5 million to settle a shareholder class action lawsuit that accused the social media company of painting an overly rosy picture of its future.  [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-09-20/twitter-in-810-million-settlement-of-shareholder-suit-on-growth?srnd=premium (Bloomberg)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 La Palma eruption]]
**More than 100 homes on the island of [[La Palma]] in the [[Spain|Spanish]] [[Canary Islands]] are destroyed by lava flows, and 5,000 people are evacuated. Several schools on the island suspend classes. [https://www.elmundo.es/ciencia-y-salud/ciencia/2021/09/20/61480a3dfc6c83bd7d8b4639.html (''El Mundo'')] [https://www.europapress.es/islas-canarias/noticia-suspenden-clases-paso-llanos-aridane-tazacorte-20210919200914.html (''Europa Press'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in England]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in the United Kingdom]]
*****[[England]] and [[Scotland]] begin the rollout of [[COVID-19 vaccine]]s for children between the ages of 12 and 15 as part of an expansion of their vaccination programme in order to protect more people from COVID-19 during the winter. [https://www.bbc.com/news/health-58623058 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Austria]]
****The [[Austria]]n [[Government of Austria|government]] announces that it will require [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|protective face mask]]s and [[Immunity passport#COVID-19|COVID-19 pass]]es for users of [[ski lift]]s this winter in order to prevent the spread of COVID-19 as the country will allow foreign skiers for the first time in two years. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/austria-will-require-masks-covid-19-passes-ski-lifts-2021-09-20/ (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Italy]]
****[[Italy]] begins administering [[booster dose]]s of the COVID-19 vaccine to clinically vulnerable people using [[Messenger RNA|mRNA]]-based vaccines.  [https://www.ansa.it/english/news/general_news/2021/09/20/covid-19-italy-starts-giving-3rd-jabs-to-vulnerable_bdaf8a24-c5f7-44ee-837b-9d973df7b609.html (ANSA)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Switzerland]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****[[Switzerland]] begins to implement a mandatory negative [[COVID-19 testing|COVID-19 test]] result for travellers who have not been vaccinated or who have not recovered from [[COVID-19]] upon entering the country in order to reduce the spread of COVID-19. [https://www.schengenvisainfo.com/news/non-vaccinated-travellers-reaching-switzerland-subjected-to-double-testing-requirement/ (Schengen Visa Info)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vatican City]]
****The [[Vatican City]] issues a decree that would require visitors who enter the [[city state]] to show an [[Italy|Italian]] Green Pass or its international [[immunity passport]] equivalent, providing proof that they have been vaccinated, tested negative in the previous 72 hours, or have recovered from COVID-19, beginning on October 1. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/religion/vatican-city-enforces-mandates-for-vaccines-covid-19-test/2021/09/20/ec3aa2b4-1a38-11ec-bea8-308ea134594f_story.html (''The Washington Post'')] [https://www.catholicnewsagency.com/news/249038/vatican-requires-vaccine-pass-for-visitors-employees (Catholic News Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C.]]
*****[[Washington, D.C.|Washington D.C.]] [[Mayor of Washington D.C.|Mayor]] [[Muriel Bowser]] announces that COVID-19 vaccines will be required for all teachers and students in the district by November 1. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/local/education/dc-school-staff-child-care-covid-vaccine-mandate/2021/09/20/771e53cc-1a10-11ec-bcb8-0cb135811007_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
****The [[Presidency of Joe Biden|Biden administration]] announces that [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic|travel restrictions]] will be lifted for international travellers who are fully vaccinated and show a negative COVID-19 test. These rules will be in effect beginning in November. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/09/20/vaccinated-travellers-from-uk-and-eu-allowed-into-us-from-november (Euronews)]
***The [[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention|CDC]] releases a study, which finds that 99.4% of all current cases of COVID-19 in the United States are of the highly transmittable [[SARS-CoV-2 lineage B.1.617|Lineage B.1.617]] [[SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant|Delta variant]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/09/18/health/delta-covid-us-cases-cdc.html (''The New York Times'')]
***The total number of deaths from COVID-19 in the [[United States|U.S.]] surpasses the total number of deaths from the [[Spanish flu]] in the U.S. from 1918 to 1919. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/covid-19-now-killed-americans-1918-19-spanish-80133187 (ABC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Uzbekistan]]
***[[Uzbekistan]] lifts some COVID-19-related restrictions, allowing the reopening of theatres, cinemas, and concert halls, as well as allowing mass events to be held indoors and outdoors due to a decline in the number of COVID-19 cases. [https://m.akipress.com/news:662663:Uzbekistan_eases_quarantine_restrictions_since_Sept_20/ (AKI Press)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***[[Pfizer]] says that [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|their vaccine]] candidate is effective for children between the ages of 5 and 11 years. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/pfizer-covid-vaccine-kids-age-5-11/ (CBS News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[El Salvador–United States relations]], [[Guatemala–United States relations]]
**[[United States Secretary of State|U.S. Secretary of State]] [[Antony Blinken]] announces that the department has included five judges of the [[Supreme Court of El Salvador]] as well as the [[Attorney General of Guatemala]] [[María Consuelo Porras]] in a list of "undemocratic and corrupt" officials. [https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/reuters/u-s--adds-top-guatemalan--salvadoran-officials-to-corruption-list/46963598 (Swissinfo)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Perm State University shooting]]
**Six people are killed and around 20 more are wounded in a [[mass shooting]] at [[Perm State University]] in [[Perm, Russia|Perm]], [[Perm Krai]], [[Russia]]. The gunman, an 18-year-old student at the university, has been arrested. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-58623160 (BBC News)]
*[[2021 Belarus–European Union border crisis]]
**[[Poland]] accuses [[Russia]] and [[Belarus]] of "orchestrating a wave of illegal immigration" after four people were found dead yesterday at the [[Belarus–Poland border|Polish–Belarusian border]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/9/20/after-four-found-dead-poland-blames-belarus-for-migrant-wave (Al Jazeera)]
*Three former [[U.S. intelligence|U.S. intelligence operatives]], who worked as senior managers at a [[United Arab Emirates]]–based company, have been ordered by the [[Department of Justice]] to pay [[US$|$]]1,685,000 in fines for "leveraging [[Zero-click attack|zero-click]] exploits to illegally obtain and use access credentials for online accounts issued by [[United States|U.S.]] companies, and to obtain unauthorized access to computers globally, including in the United States". [https://www.foxbusiness.com/politics/former-us-intel-personnel-fined-providing-hacking-services (Fox Business News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Canadian federal election]]
**Voters in [[Canada]] go to the polls to elect members of the House of Commons to the 44th Canadian Parliament, with pollsters predicting a tight race between [[Justin Trudeau]]'s incumbent Liberal Party and [[Erin O'Toole]]'s opposition Conservative Party. [https://www.ctvnews.ca/politics/federal-election-2021/election-day-2021-canadians-to-decide-who-will-lead-the-country-1.5592137 (CTV News)]
**The [[Liberal Party of Canada|Liberal Party]] is projected to retain their minority government. [https://www.ctvnews.ca/politics/federal-election-2021/liberals-win-minority-government-in-2021-federal-election-1.5592137 (CTV News)]
**O'Toole speaks to supporters and announces that he has made a phone call to Trudeau to concede the election. [https://nationalpost.com/pmn/news-pmn/canadas-main-opposition-party-concedes-defeat-after-pm-trudeau-wins-third-term (''National Post'')]
**The [[Conservative Party of Canada|Conservative Party]] win a plurality of the popular vote for the second consecutive election. [https://ca.style.yahoo.com/erin-otoole-conservatives-popular-vote-canada-election-054033279.html (Yahoo! News Canada)]
*Aftermath of the [[17 October Revolution]]
**The [[parliament of Lebanon]] approves the [[Third Cabinet of Najib Mikati|government]] formed by [[Prime Minister of Lebanon|Prime Minister]] [[Najib Mikati]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210920-lawmakers-in-crisis-hit-lebanon-vote-in-new-government (AFP via France 24)]
*[[COVID-19 protests in Australia]]
**Members of [[Melbourne]]'s [[Far-right politics in Australia|far-right]] violate [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown laws]] and riot at the office of the [[Construction, Forestry, Maritime, Mining and Energy Union]], damaging windows and assaulting state secretary [[John Setka]] before being dispersed by police. The rioters were dressed in the [[high-visibility clothing]] associated with the construction industry and presented themselves as Union rank-and-file protesting a bureaucracy which they claimed was working to impose [[Vaccination policy|mandatory COVID-19 vaccination]]s. Setka said that the Union opposes mandatory vaccinations and blamed the riots on "outside extremists", stating that only a minority of those in attendance were Union members. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/sep/20/construction-union-blames-extremists-as-melbourne-protest-against-vaccine-mandate-turns-violent (''The Guardian'')]
